relationships.description: The media-type entry groups the per-property serialization rules that govern how each top-level schema property becomes a part of its multipart or form-urlencoded payload.
relationships.evidence: The MediaType object under a requestBody's content map (e.g. multipart/form-data) has an `encoding` map whose keys match top-level property names of its schema.

relationships.description: The media-type entry collects named sample payloads in its `examples` map, each illustrating one concrete body sent or returned with that MIME type, and those samples may also be reused elsewhere.
relationships.evidence: The MediaType object declares an `examples` map whose named entries are inline Example objects or $refs into components/examples.

relationships.description: The media-type entry is indirectly related to part-level header declarations that its encoding rules attach to individual multipart parts.
relationships.evidence: An Encoding entry inside the MediaType's `encoding` map declares a `headers` map (e.g. X-Rate-Limit or Content-Disposition details) for a multipart part.

relationships.description: Each encoding rule exists only as an entry of this media type's `encoding` map, so the per-property serialization rule has no meaning outside the multipart or form body it shapes.
relationships.evidence: The OpenAPI document nests an Encoding object directly under `content.<mime>.encoding.<propertyName>` with no components registry or $ref form available for it.

relationships.description: The media-type entry owns an inline schema that defines the shape of the payload carried with that MIME type, and that schema exists only within this content entry.
relationships.evidence: The MediaType object's `schema` field contains an inline Schema object (type, properties, required) rather than a $ref.

relationships.description: The media-type entry points to a reusable sample payload registered in components so that the shared example illustrates this content type without being redefined.
relationships.evidence: An entry in the MediaType's `examples` map is `$ref: '#/components/examples/<Name>'`.

relationships.description: The media-type entry takes its payload shape from a named, reusable schema defined in components rather than defining that shape inline.
The media-type entry supplies one acceptable MIME-type variant of the payload a client may send in an operation's request body.
relationships.evidence: The RequestBody object's `content` map contains this MediaType keyed by a MIME type such as application/json or multipart/form-data.

relationships.description: The media-type entry supplies one MIME-type representation of the body returned for a given status code of an operation.
relationships.evidence: The Response object's `content` map contains this MediaType keyed by a MIME type such as application/json.

notes: aggregates and composes encoding are contradictory; Encoding cannot exist outside its MediaType, so keep composes only. associated-with header is indirect (via Encoding) and redundant. serves requestbody/response misstates structure: RequestBody and Response compose MediaType through their content map; use the inverse composed-of instead.
